headline: High-risk shared-network pair: open-webui can ingest and act on dexter outputs, creating default prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dexter can emit autonomous research outputs and uses files plus broad network egress; open-webui supports MCP, plugins, and function calling, so it can ingest external content by default. The pair lacks documented provenance/isolation, so prompt injection is plausible even though no shared channel is explicitly proven. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF open-webui imports dexter-generated text into chat, MCP, or a tool prompt without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF dexter writes attacker-controlled content into .dexter/scratchpad/ and open-webui reads it, the bridge exists.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of dexter outputs into open-webui prompts.
Require provenance tags on any file or message passed between the agents.
Restrict open-webui tool execution for content sourced from dexter.
Use separate workspaces or volumes for each agent.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist filters at the handoff boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter handles financial and market data and has broad network egress; open-webui touches files, persistent memory, API keys, and can call many external APIs. If they share a workspace or session path, sensitive data can flow from dexter into open-webui and then onward to third-party services, creating a realistic exfiltration path in default-style deployments.
conditions: IF both agents share any filesystem, mounted volume, or copied scratchpad content, dexter data can reach open-webui.
IF open-webui forwards imported context to external APIs, the leakage extends beyond the local pair.
mitigations: Keep dexter and open-webui on separate volumes.
Block open-webui from reading dexter scratchpad paths.
Disable external API connectors for any session containing dexter data.
Rotate any API keys exposed in shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention at the orchestrator boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dexter has broad network egress and autonomous execution, while open-webui can run browsers, spawn subprocesses, and use MCP/OpenAPI tools. Both support multiple instances and can write to files, so overlapping writes and concurrent side effects are plausible. Without locking or coordination, the pair can race on shared mutable resources and corrupt state.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory, repo, or mounted data volume, write conflicts can occur.
IF open-webui uses shared Redis/session state while dexter writes related artifacts, concurrent mutation is possible.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate writable directory.
Serialize access to any shared repo or volume.
Disable subprocess/browser actions in open-webui for shared targets.
Run one agent at a time on mutable resources.
requires-engineering: add distributed locking around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: dexter produces autonomous research outputs that open-webui can readily consume through chat, tools, or MCP. Because open-webui supports function calling and external tool execution, it may treat dexter output as authoritative and act on it without verification. That creates a direct path from generated facts to downstream actions, with potentially irreversible consequences.
conditions: IF open-webui uses dexter output as tool arguments, citations, or instructions without verification, cascading error occurs.
IF open-webui is configured to send emails, edit files, or call APIs based on dexter-produced content, the blast radius becomes operational.
mitigations: Require human review before any action based on dexter output.
Add a verification step that cross-checks dexter claims against sources.
Disable autonomous tool execution for dexter-originated content.
Log and flag all dexter-to-open-webui handoffs.
requires-engineering: implement policy gates for action-taking tools.

E_compliance.rationale: dexter touches financial data and market data, while open-webui handles persistent memory, files, API keys, and can route data through external APIs. If regulated financial data is moved into open-webui’s broader storage or third-party connectors, retention and residency controls may diverge. The pairwise compliance risk is therefore a plausible mismatch, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF financial data from dexter is stored in open-webui persistent memory or files, retention policy mismatch is possible.
IF open-webui sends that data to external APIs without a DPA or residency controls, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of open-webui memory and files.
Disable external connectors for regulated sessions.
Set short retention on any shared artifacts.
Review data-flow and residency settings before use.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows across both systems.
